Over gzip: the same 3.
Over a gzip-compressed event stream: the same 3.

steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: A tool that does not exist gets the identical refusal.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: sam.jones has no policy on ledger: even initialize is refused (deny by default).
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Prompts are filtered too: staff see one of two.
Resources too: staff see one of three.
Reading a resource staff may not see is refused.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Reading a resource staff may see works.
A JSON-RPC method the gateway does not recognise is refused: the method is part of the decision.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: priya.nair grants staff export_all on ledger.
It now appears in the listing and can be called.

steps.say: YAML is refused: JSON only.
steps.detail: JSON only: the lab does not parse YAML or anything else

steps.say: priya.nair deploys the specification as an application.
Staff see only the read-only operations (the lab default grant).
Call getItem: the path parameter drives the request to the mock backend.
A mutating operation is hidden from staff and refused.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Arguments are checked against the generated schema: a wrong type is refused.
steps.detail: the arguments do not match the tool's input schema (must be an integer)

steps.say: priya.nair redeploys the specification with the DELETE operation removed.
The removed operation is gone for everyone, administrators included.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

scenarios.title: Five ways to inject a backend credential
scenarios.say: The agent never holds the credential. A static token makes everyone the same service account; a vault credential, a second OAuth flow and a signed assertion let the backend see the person. The assertion is real RS256 and is verified twice.

steps.say: ledger has an app-wide static token, so the backend sees only a service account, not maya.chen.
priya.nair switches ledger to the per-user vault.
omar.reyes has no vault credential for ledger: refused before the backend is called.
steps.detail: this user has no credential for this application in the User Vault

steps.say: priya.nair cannot set omar.reyes's vault entry: the vault is self-service, with no administrator override.
steps.detail: a vault entry can only be set by the user it belongs to: there is no administrator override

steps.say: omar.reyes stores their own.
Now the backend sees omar.reyes and scopes the answer to them.
cases uses a second OAuth flow, per user: maya.chen has not authorized it yet.
steps.detail: this user has not authorized the member's own OAuth server yet

steps.say: maya.chen authorizes the member's own server.
The call now works.
Twenty minutes later the access token has expired: it is refreshed on the next call.
Still works.
priya.nair switches payments to token pass-through.
A valid assertion: the gateway verifies and forwards it unchanged; the backend verifies it too and scopes to maya.chen.
A wrong audience is refused by the gateway.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (wrong_audience)

steps.say: An expired assertion is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (expired)

steps.say: A tampered payload fails the signature.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (bad_signature)

steps.say: An untrusted issuer is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (untrusted_issuer)

steps.say: alg "none" is refused: one algorithm is accepted.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (alg_not_allowed)

steps.say: A lifetime over the cap is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (lifetime_too_long)

steps.say: A replay: the first presentation was accepted, the second is refused by the backend.
steps.detail: the backend refused the assertion: this jti was already used (replay)

scenarios.title: The catalog: a verified server in one step, operated and redeployed
scenarios.say: A verified catalog entry deploys as a namespaced managed container with policy, credential injection and audit in place before the first request. Unknown and unverified entries are refused. A crash is found by a health check, and a configuration change redeploys.

The very first request already has the policy: staff see the read-only tools.
And the first call is authorized, injected and audited.
An unknown entry is refused.
steps.detail: no such catalog entry

steps.say: An unverified entry is refused.
steps.detail: this entry is not verified, so it cannot be deployed

steps.say: The same name in the same tenant namespace is refused.
steps.detail: a deployment with this name already exists in this tenant namespace

steps.say: The same name in another tenant's namespace is fine: containers are namespaced per tenant.
The container exits.
Before a health check notices, a call fails at the connect.
steps.detail: the container is not running (not yet detected by a health check)

steps.say: The health check marks it unhealthy.
Calls are refused while it is unhealthy.
steps.detail: the deployment is not healthy

steps.say: Redeploy: it is healthy again, one generation later.
A configuration change redeploys it.
The same configuration again changes nothing, so nothing redeploys.
steps.detail: the configuration is unchanged, so nothing is redeployed

steps.say: Customer-published entries are on the roadmap: refused.
steps.detail: customer-published catalog entries are on the roadmap (deck claim): nothing is modelled

scenarios.title: OAuth 2.1 with mandatory PKCE, refresh tokens and CIMD
scenarios.say: Dynamic registration, PKCE S256 verified for real, single-use codes and rotating refresh tokens; and CIMD, where the client is named by a document URL the tenant has allowlisted. The lab never fetches: each URL has one fixed mock outcome.

steps.say: Register a client dynamically.
An authorization request with no PKCE challenge is refused.
steps.detail: PKCE is mandatory: send a code_challenge (43 base64url characters)

steps.say: The "plain" method is refused: S256 only.
steps.detail: only code_challenge_method S256 is accepted ("plain" and a missing method are refused)

steps.say: A redirect URI that does not match exactly is refused.
steps.detail: the redirect URI does not exactly match a registered one

steps.say: A valid request with S256 gets a single-use code.
A wrong code_verifier fails PKCE (the hash does not match).
steps.detail: PKCE verification failed: base64url(sha256(code_verifier)) does not equal the code_challenge

steps.say: The right verifier exchanges the code for an access token and a refresh token.
Using the same code again is refused, and revokes what it issued.
steps.detail: the authorization code was already used: the tokens issued from it are revoked

steps.say: The refresh token was revoked with its family: refreshing fails.
steps.detail: unknown, revoked or expired refresh token

steps.say: A new code, a new exchange.
Exchange it.
Refresh: a rotated pair is issued.
Presenting the old refresh token again is reuse: the whole family is revoked.
steps.detail: a refresh token that was already used was presented again: the whole token family is revoked

steps.say: CIMD: a client_id that is not an https URL is refused.
steps.detail: a client ID metadata URL must be https

steps.say: A URL the tenant has not allowlisted is refused.
steps.detail: the tenant has not allowlisted this client ID metadata URL

steps.say: An allowlisted document is fetched (a fixed mock), validated and cached.
The second resolution is a cache hit: no fetch.
A document whose client_id is not its own URL is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_client_id_mismatch)

steps.say: A document over the size limit is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_too_large)

steps.say: Refused: a document that asks for a symmetric client credential.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_symmetric_secret_refused)

steps.say: A wrong content type is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_wrong_content_type)

steps.say: A fetch that times out is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_fetch_timeout)

steps.say: A redirect is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_redirect_refused)

steps.say: A document whose redirect URI is off the reserved hosts is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_bad_redirect_uri)

steps.say: A day passes: the cache entry has expired and the document is fetched again.
The second fetch.

scenarios.title: Approval-gated creation, session logging, headless agents and hosting
scenarios.say: Nothing is created until an administrator approves; nobody decides their own proposal; a denied proposal cannot be approved; a changed proposal is stale. Session logging records invocations; a headless agent acts as its owner; one hostname serves every application by path, and sessions must be pinned to a replica.

steps.say: maya.chen proposes a new MCP application.
maya.chen cannot approve it.
steps.detail: only a tenant administrator may do this

steps.say: priya.nair proposes one too, then tries to approve their own.
Self-approval is refused, administrators included.
steps.detail: nobody decides their own proposal

steps.say: maya.chen amends the first proposal after lee.park has looked at revision 1.
lee.park approves revision 1: stale, refused.
steps.detail: the proposal changed after you looked at it: review the new revision

steps.say: lee.park approves revision 2 and adjusts the name.
lee.park denies the second proposal.
A denied proposal cannot be approved afterwards.
steps.detail: a denied proposal cannot be approved: propose again

steps.say: priya.nair switches session logging on.
A call is recorded with its arguments.
The headless agent recon-bot calls as its owner maya.chen.
An agent key scoped for llm only is refused for MCP.
steps.detail: this key is not scoped for mcp access (measured wording, AI-DEMO2 note)

steps.say: priya.nair revokes the agent.
A revoked agent is refused.
steps.detail: this agent has been revoked

steps.say: One hostname, addressed by path: a path resolves to one application.
A path nobody serves is a 404.
steps.detail: no application is served on this path

steps.say: maya.chen opens a session on replica A.
The next request lands on replica B, which holds no state for it.
steps.detail: this replica holds no state for the session: its OAuth state lives on the replica that opened it, so the client must be pinned

steps.say: priya.nair pins client sessions to a replica.
The same request now reaches the replica that holds the session.

steps.say: Preview the sample specification: four operations, one named by the fallback rule.
A remote reference is refused.
steps.detail: only local "#/" references are resolved: remote, file and relative references are refused

steps.say: YAML is refused: JSON only.
steps.detail: JSON only: the lab does not parse YAML or anything else

steps.say: grace.liu deploys the specification as an application.
Staff see only the read-only operations (the lab default grant).
Call getItem: the path parameter drives the request to the mock backend.
A mutating operation is hidden from staff and refused.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Arguments are checked against the generated schema: a wrong type is refused.
steps.detail: the arguments do not match the tool's input schema (must be an integer)

steps.say: grace.liu redeploys the specification with the DELETE operation removed.
The removed operation is gone for everyone, administrators included.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

scenarios.title: Five ways to inject a backend credential
scenarios.say: The agent never holds the credential. A static token makes everyone the same service account; a vault credential, a second OAuth flow and a signed assertion let the backend see the person. The assertion is real RS256 and is verified twice.

steps.say: records has an app-wide static token, so the backend sees only a service account, not lena.ortiz.
grace.liu switches records to the per-user vault.
tariq.hassan has no vault credential for records: refused before the backend is called.
steps.detail: this user has no credential for this application in the User Vault

steps.say: grace.liu cannot set tariq.hassan's vault entry: the vault is self-service, with no administrator override.
steps.detail: a vault entry can only be set by the user it belongs to: there is no administrator override

steps.say: tariq.hassan stores their own.
Now the backend sees tariq.hassan and scopes the answer to them.
triage uses a second OAuth flow, per user: lena.ortiz has not authorized it yet.
steps.detail: this user has not authorized the member's own OAuth server yet

steps.say: lena.ortiz authorizes the member's own server.
The call now works.
Twenty minutes later the access token has expired: it is refreshed on the next call.
Still works.
grace.liu switches claims to token pass-through.
A valid assertion: the gateway verifies and forwards it unchanged; the backend verifies it too and scopes to lena.ortiz.
A wrong audience is refused by the gateway.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (wrong_audience)

steps.say: An expired assertion is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (expired)

steps.say: A tampered payload fails the signature.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (bad_signature)

steps.say: An untrusted issuer is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (untrusted_issuer)

steps.say: alg "none" is refused: one algorithm is accepted.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (alg_not_allowed)

steps.say: A lifetime over the cap is refused.
steps.detail: the gateway refused the assertion (lifetime_too_long)

steps.say: A replay: the first presentation was accepted, the second is refused by the backend.
steps.detail: the backend refused the assertion: this jti was already used (replay)

scenarios.title: The catalog: a verified server in one step, operated and redeployed
scenarios.say: A verified catalog entry deploys as a namespaced managed container with policy, credential injection and audit in place before the first request. Unknown and unverified entries are refused. A crash is found by a health check, and a configuration change redeploys.

steps.say: grace.liu deploys the verified "kb-search" entry in one step.
The very first request already has the policy: staff see the read-only tools.
And the first call is authorized, injected and audited.
An unknown entry is refused.
steps.detail: no such catalog entry

steps.say: An unverified entry is refused.
steps.detail: this entry is not verified, so it cannot be deployed

steps.say: The same name in the same tenant namespace is refused.
steps.detail: a deployment with this name already exists in this tenant namespace

steps.say: The same name in another tenant's namespace is fine: containers are namespaced per tenant.
The container exits.
Before a health check notices, a call fails at the connect.
steps.detail: the container is not running (not yet detected by a health check)

steps.say: The health check marks it unhealthy.
Calls are refused while it is unhealthy.
steps.detail: the deployment is not healthy

steps.say: Redeploy: it is healthy again, one generation later.
A configuration change redeploys it.
The same configuration again changes nothing, so nothing redeploys.
steps.detail: the configuration is unchanged, so nothing is redeployed

steps.say: Customer-published entries are on the roadmap: refused.
steps.detail: customer-published catalog entries are on the roadmap (deck claim): nothing is modelled

scenarios.title: OAuth 2.1 with mandatory PKCE, refresh tokens and CIMD
scenarios.say: Dynamic registration, PKCE S256 verified for real, single-use codes and rotating refresh tokens; and CIMD, where the client is named by a document URL the tenant has allowlisted. The lab never fetches: each URL has one fixed mock outcome.

steps.say: Register a client dynamically.
An authorization request with no PKCE challenge is refused.
steps.detail: PKCE is mandatory: send a code_challenge (43 base64url characters)

steps.say: The "plain" method is refused: S256 only.
steps.detail: only code_challenge_method S256 is accepted ("plain" and a missing method are refused)

steps.say: A redirect URI that does not match exactly is refused.
steps.detail: the redirect URI does not exactly match a registered one

steps.say: A valid request with S256 gets a single-use code.
A wrong code_verifier fails PKCE (the hash does not match).
steps.detail: PKCE verification failed: base64url(sha256(code_verifier)) does not equal the code_challenge

steps.say: The right verifier exchanges the code for an access token and a refresh token.
Using the same code again is refused, and revokes what it issued.
steps.detail: the authorization code was already used: the tokens issued from it are revoked

steps.say: The refresh token was revoked with its family: refreshing fails.
steps.detail: unknown, revoked or expired refresh token

steps.say: A new code, a new exchange.
Exchange it.
Refresh: a rotated pair is issued.
Presenting the old refresh token again is reuse: the whole family is revoked.
steps.detail: a refresh token that was already used was presented again: the whole token family is revoked

steps.say: CIMD: a client_id that is not an https URL is refused.
steps.detail: a client ID metadata URL must be https

steps.say: A URL the tenant has not allowlisted is refused.
steps.detail: the tenant has not allowlisted this client ID metadata URL

steps.say: An allowlisted document is fetched (a fixed mock), validated and cached.
The second resolution is a cache hit: no fetch.
A document whose client_id is not its own URL is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_client_id_mismatch)

steps.say: A document over the size limit is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_too_large)

steps.say: Refused: a document that asks for a symmetric client credential.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_symmetric_secret_refused)

steps.say: A wrong content type is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_wrong_content_type)

steps.say: A fetch that times out is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_fetch_timeout)

steps.say: A redirect is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_redirect_refused)

steps.say: A document whose redirect URI is off the reserved hosts is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_bad_redirect_uri)

steps.say: A day passes: the cache entry has expired and the document is fetched again.
The second fetch.

scenarios.title: Approval-gated creation, session logging, headless agents and hosting
scenarios.say: Nothing is created until an administrator approves; nobody decides their own proposal; a denied proposal cannot be approved; a changed proposal is stale. Session logging records invocations; a headless agent acts as its owner; one hostname serves every application by path, and sessions must be pinned to a replica.

steps.say: lena.ortiz proposes a new MCP application.
lena.ortiz cannot approve it.
steps.detail: only a tenant administrator may do this

steps.say: grace.liu proposes one too, then tries to approve their own.
Self-approval is refused, administrators included.
steps.detail: nobody decides their own proposal

steps.say: lena.ortiz amends the first proposal after kofi.mensah has looked at revision 1.
kofi.mensah approves revision 1: stale, refused.
steps.detail: the proposal changed after you looked at it: review the new revision

steps.say: kofi.mensah approves revision 2 and adjusts the name.
kofi.mensah denies the second proposal.
A denied proposal cannot be approved afterwards.
steps.detail: a denied proposal cannot be approved: propose again

steps.say: grace.liu switches session logging on.
A call is recorded with its arguments.
The headless agent intake-bot calls as its owner lena.ortiz.
An agent key scoped for llm only is refused for MCP.
steps.detail: this key is not scoped for mcp access (measured wording, AI-DEMO2 note)

steps.say: grace.liu revokes the agent.
A revoked agent is refused.
steps.detail: this agent has been revoked

steps.say: One hostname, addressed by path: a path resolves to one application.
A path nobody serves is a 404.
steps.detail: no application is served on this path

steps.say: lena.ortiz opens a session on replica A.
The next request lands on replica B, which holds no state for it.
steps.detail: this replica holds no state for the session: its OAuth state lives on the replica that opened it, so the client must be pinned

steps.say: grace.liu pins client sessions to a replica.
The same request now reaches the replica that holds the session.

scenarios.title: The aggregate's policy is the cap, enforced twice
scenarios.say: One endpoint fronts stock, checkout, returns, loyalty and legacy-pos. A tool the member allows but the aggregate denies is hidden and refused at the aggregate; a tool the aggregate allows but the member denies is refused at the member hop. Each fault switch shows one layer alone is enough.

steps.say: diego.ruiz lists tools through the aggregate: namespaced names, only what the aggregate permits and the member allows.
checkout__create_item: the member allows it for staff, the aggregate's policy does not. Refused at the aggregate.
steps.detail: access denied

steps.say: checkout__refund_item: the aggregate allows it, the member does not. Refused at the member hop.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: stock__read_record: allowed by both. The call goes through, with the static token the member's auth mode injects.
olu.adeyemi switches off the aggregate's own check (a lab fault switch).
The same create_item call is still refused: the second enforcement, at the member hop, carries the aggregate's cap.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: olu.adeyemi also makes the member hop ignore the cap header.
With both layers broken the call goes through: the aggregate is wider than its own policy. This is why the cap is enforced twice.
Both switches off again.

scenarios.title: Aliases, lazy connections and members that are missing, down or hang
scenarios.say: Members are resolved from the tenant's own applications and connected only when a tool is called. A missing or unreachable member is reported, not dropped; a member recorded as sse hangs (a measured note). An alias clash is refused, and renaming an alias strands the old grant.

steps.say: A listing connects nothing: every member reports "not connected yet", the down one "unreachable" and the dangling reference "missing".
A first call to stock connects it (one connection).
A second call reuses the connection: one connect, two calls.
loyalty is down: the call fails with the reason, named after the member.
steps.detail: loyalty: the member is unreachable

steps.say: legacy-pos is recorded as sse: the call never answers (the lab times it out at a simulated 30 seconds).
steps.detail: legacy-pos: the member did not answer within the lab's simulated 30 seconds

steps.say: pricing-old does not exist: reported as missing.
steps.detail: pricing-old: the member application does not exist

steps.say: olu.adeyemi records legacy-pos as streamable-http (the measured fix was a 405-on-GET front).
The same call now answers.
A bare tool name with no alias is refused.
steps.detail: the tool name is not namespaced; expected <alias>__<tool>

steps.say: olu.adeyemi tries to give stock the alias of checkout: identical tool names would collide.
steps.detail: another member already uses this alias: identical tool names would collide

steps.say: olu.adeyemi renames stock to "books". Its old grant now matches nothing.
A call by the old name is refused: that prefix is no longer a member alias.
steps.detail: unknown server: the prefix is not a member alias

scenarios.title: Entitlement-aware discovery: removed in flight, never callable
scenarios.say: The upstream lists everything. The gateway filters the listing in flight on a plain body, on a stream split into small chunks with comments and notifications, and on gzip. A tool you may not see cannot be called, and the refusal is the same as for one that does not exist.

steps.say: diego.ruiz lists stock's tools: 3 of 5.
The same listing over a chunked event stream: the same 3.
Over gzip: the same 3.
Over a gzip-compressed event stream: the same 3.
A hidden tool cannot be called.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: A tool that does not exist gets the identical refusal.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: mia.kowalski has no policy on stock: even initialize is refused (deny by default).
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Prompts are filtered too: staff see one of two.
Resources too: staff see one of three.
Reading a resource staff may not see is refused.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: Reading a resource staff may see works.
A JSON-RPC method the gateway does not recognise is refused: the method is part of the decision.
steps.detail: access denied: the request is not permitted by policy

steps.say: olu.adeyemi grants staff export_all on stock.
It now appears in the listing and can be called.

scenarios.title: OAuth 2.1 with mandatory PKCE, refresh tokens and CIMD
scenarios.say: Dynamic registration, PKCE S256 verified for real, single-use codes and rotating refresh tokens; and CIMD, where the client is named by a document URL the tenant has allowlisted. The lab never fetches: each URL has one fixed mock outcome.

steps.say: Register a client dynamically.
An authorization request with no PKCE challenge is refused.
steps.detail: PKCE is mandatory: send a code_challenge (43 base64url characters)

steps.say: The "plain" method is refused: S256 only.
steps.detail: only code_challenge_method S256 is accepted ("plain" and a missing method are refused)

steps.say: A redirect URI that does not match exactly is refused.
steps.detail: the redirect URI does not exactly match a registered one

steps.say: A valid request with S256 gets a single-use code.
A wrong code_verifier fails PKCE (the hash does not match).
steps.detail: PKCE verification failed: base64url(sha256(code_verifier)) does not equal the code_challenge

steps.say: The right verifier exchanges the code for an access token and a refresh token.
Using the same code again is refused, and revokes what it issued.
steps.detail: the authorization code was already used: the tokens issued from it are revoked

steps.say: The refresh token was revoked with its family: refreshing fails.
steps.detail: unknown, revoked or expired refresh token

steps.say: A new code, a new exchange.
Exchange it.
Refresh: a rotated pair is issued.
Presenting the old refresh token again is reuse: the whole family is revoked.
steps.detail: a refresh token that was already used was presented again: the whole token family is revoked

steps.say: CIMD: a client_id that is not an https URL is refused.
steps.detail: a client ID metadata URL must be https

steps.say: A URL the tenant has not allowlisted is refused.
steps.detail: the tenant has not allowlisted this client ID metadata URL

steps.say: An allowlisted document is fetched (a fixed mock), validated and cached.
The second resolution is a cache hit: no fetch.
A document whose client_id is not its own URL is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_client_id_mismatch)

steps.say: A document over the size limit is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_too_large)

steps.say: Refused: a document that asks for a symmetric client credential.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_symmetric_secret_refused)

steps.say: A wrong content type is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_wrong_content_type)

steps.say: A fetch that times out is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_fetch_timeout)

steps.say: A redirect is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_redirect_refused)

steps.say: A document whose redirect URI is off the reserved hosts is refused.
steps.detail: the client document was refused (cimd_bad_redirect_uri)

steps.say: A day passes: the cache entry has expired and the document is fetched again.
The second fetch.

scenarios.title: Approval-gated creation, session logging, headless agents and hosting
scenarios.say: Nothing is created until an administrator approves; nobody decides their own proposal; a denied proposal cannot be approved; a changed proposal is stale. Session logging records invocations; a headless agent acts as its owner; one hostname serves every application by path, and sessions must be pinned to a replica.

steps.say: diego.ruiz proposes a new MCP application.
diego.ruiz cannot approve it.
steps.detail: only a tenant administrator may do this

steps.say: olu.adeyemi proposes one too, then tries to approve their own.
Self-approval is refused, administrators included.
steps.detail: nobody decides their own proposal

steps.say: diego.ruiz amends the first proposal after anna.berg has looked at revision 1.
anna.berg approves revision 1: stale, refused.
steps.detail: the proposal changed after you looked at it: review the new revision

steps.say: anna.berg approves revision 2 and adjusts the name.
anna.berg denies the second proposal.
A denied proposal cannot be approved afterwards.
steps.detail: a denied proposal cannot be approved: propose again

steps.say: olu.adeyemi switches session logging on.
A call is recorded with its arguments.
The headless agent stock-bot calls as its owner diego.ruiz.
An agent key scoped for llm only is refused for MCP.
steps.detail: this key is not scoped for mcp access (measured wording, AI-DEMO2 note)

steps.say: olu.adeyemi revokes the agent.
A revoked agent is refused.
steps.detail: this agent has been revoked

steps.say: One hostname, addressed by path: a path resolves to one application.
A path nobody serves is a 404.
steps.detail: no application is served on this path

steps.say: diego.ruiz opens a session on replica A.
The next request lands on replica B, which holds no state for it.
steps.detail: this replica holds no state for the session: its OAuth state lives on the replica that opened it, so the client must be pinned

steps.say: olu.adeyemi pins client sessions to a replica.
The same request now reaches the replica that holds the session.
